about: The allowed exceptions of the import-rules ratchet (packages/core/test/import-rules.test.ts, rules in scripts/audit/lib.mjs). Each group has one rule, a one-line reason and its entries ("<file> → <import>"). A new entry and a stale one both fail the test: after a change, run node scripts/audit/rules.mjs . --write-baseline, write the reason of any new group, and review the diff.

groups.reason: CLI commands drive the adapters themselves (doctor, sign-in checks) until they run on the engine operations.
The Studio's player bundles the compositions with the components and the editor's render entry.
The Studio server reads the component library, themes and edit plans through the adapters until the engine exposes them.
CLI commands read and write files or start processes themselves (init, validate, ui, doctor) until they go through the engine.
The Studio server watches folders, serves files and supervises its worker itself.

P1: the engine still builds these adapters itself; each port (U6) removes entries. 1 file → specifier pair on 2026-11-12 (L7.11: hooks and review/thumbs went through their ports; L7.12: the runner package through the capture runner's; L7.25: the sandbox package through the Sandboxes port, its OS utilities from core/io): components 1.

Two imports of a later context, measured when the contexts were drawn (L7.35): the scenario's checks read the default theme's component names (template-defaults, theme) to check a scenario's components, and a script's draft checks its page paths with the inspection's grammar (inspectPathProblem, run). Each goes when that value moves below the scenario context (a follow-up of U10).
The journal's warn rate limit (append-log.ts logWarner): a process-wide helper with no clock in reach, compared with itself, never written; its test moves Date.now.
Memo lifetimes kept in memory only (the board's and the scenario view's caches, the Studio's one-time bootstrap codes): compared with the time they were made, never written.
File times: a filming marker's heartbeat and the library cache's recency are compared with the mtimes other processes leave, so they follow the machine's own time.
Outside the engine's contexts: the app set-up (`retake app`, the desktop app) has no composition root of the engine; its backup name takes an injectable `now` already.

Reads of a project folder through the media storage (R-ARC-03), not authored writes: a run's status, a scenario's text (14 callers), a thread view's scenario text, the search index's small files. They move when project reads get a port.

agent-written.ts reads the workspaces of an agent's write and a scenario's hooks for `retake hooks trust` on core io's loaders: the file belongs to the lot in flight beside this one (L7.39), switched onto the port after it lands
the in-memory reviewer stands for the review package, which loads the project a review names by slug itself (core io loadProject, outside the engine): the fake does what the adapter does

The renderer port still borrows the editor's and the components' types (the registry, bundle components, preview specs, render progress: L7.1 and L7.2, left), until they have a home in core or a domain entry.

The Studio's own ops (18 in 6 files on 2026-11-12, after L7.14 moved its ten read-only queries, L7.17 its eleven theme and library ops, L7.15 its six submits and job controls, L7.16 its twelve comment ops and L7.18 scenario_edit and its seven record ops): every use case the engine serves is its operation now; these hold the server's own state (its index, player, leases, set-up and update state, unsaved tabs, the desktop pipe) and stay here.
Test defaults of the job queue adapters' constructors (the roots hand theirs through the ports' queue factory, as with their clock).

This process's own environment, on purpose: the captures folder's test-run guard reads it beside the environment handed (a test that hands a clean one still never uses the per-user folder); the two `ps` runs get it with the C locale (a subprocess inherits this process's environment; yield.ts parses the start times `ps` prints in this process's time zone).

doctor's system probes run every program they check (ffmpeg and ffprobe -version, a VideoToolbox test encode, docker, git, ps) through one exec probe it hands its checks (their test seam): a shell's check of the machine, not a media run (S4 later).
Paths spelt as text on purpose: the trust lists (agent-writable paths, a person's files), a new project's .gitignore lines, help texts and the Studio's browser code (no node:path there).

Other names with a grammar of the same shape, each written at its definition and out of the id module: a scenario name (SLUG_RE), a project slug (PROJECT_SLUG_RE), an environment name, a run-folder segment, a review file id.
Hand-written mirrors of the scenario-name and project-slug grammars in the Studio front end, which imports types only: not ids of the module; one home for those two names in the app is later work.
The file suffixes of the export formats (`<render id>-vertical.mp4`, `-square.mp4`), not the variant suffix of a render id.
The new-theme grammar without its cap, on purpose: the names inside stale work folders of earlier theme creations, which must be cleaned whatever their length.

The record corpus (core/test/fixtures/records: run and render records as data, their README, and the three builders that write them into a workspace) stays one folder of core's test data: the builders read their data beside them, and the characterization tests of every package build their states from it unchanged; moving the builders to the shared helpers would split the corpus from its data, moving the corpus would move the fixtures.

The Studio's operations built with stand-ins (ui/test/studio-tools.ts) call the Studio server's own studioTools, which @retake/ui does not export: the shared helpers would reach into ui's sources instead; the engine's and MCP's tests read the op definitions through it.
The shared home helper's own test (the canary of the test environment): it keeps the run's home by hand, so that a broken helper cannot leave its own test's home behind.

groups.reason: Prune reads the run folders through the reader (L7.7) and keeps its lenient read for one case: a run.json the reader does not take as a record (a finished run without its end, a failed one without its error, a linked file) is still read as any object with a text id and status, so that a take prune could delete before the lot can still be deleted — leaving such a take alone is a change nobody decided. Where this read is stricter than before it only keeps: a file of a newer format is left alone, one that is no regular file or is over the reader's cap is not read. Its second read (L7.6b) is of renders/: a record file that is a link is not opened by the one reader of renders/, and is read through the link for the id, the take, the scenario and the creation time it says — never taken as a record — so that a linked record keeps the render and the take it kept before the lot.
entries: packages/engine/src/prune.ts → 2 own reads of a run folder's or renders/'s file

groups.reason: A reserved run is closed from outside on a lenient read of its run.json (its status alone decides): a record the reader refuses must still be closed, or it would say running for ever.
